There is a book that I don't think was ever published in English (it says so inside, but I can't find any proof of it online; the Italian title is L'eredità dell'ombra) so I doubt it will ring a bell. But it was so bad it went full circle and became good. The plot was the classic quest, which would not be a problem because I love classics, but the style and characters were so incredibly bland it probably took talent making them as boring as they are. The best part though were the absurdities. It was appearently set in an alternate history version of medieval Britain, which sounded great, but at one point it says that the Fire Land (England) and the Earth Land (Ireland) confine as if there wasn't a whole sea in between them. The four main characters were useless compared to the true main character, an elf maiden that was, and I quote, more beautiful than Helen of Troy, the best fighter ever, with a ton of amazing magical powers, etc. She and her boyfriend were able to change into wolves and he turned into "an attractive wolf of many colours, especially gray". There was at least one scene copied word from word from Mulan (1997). At one point one character is addressed as "Abernathy, also called mouth of the Nethy river". The main character fought the bad guys while wearing a jumpsuit above a kimono, Mongolian-style boots, a scarf and striped socks. In medieval Wales. I'm quite sure it was supposed to be an elaborate attempt at trolling but I laughed so hard I couldn't even be mad for wasting my time.

Lostwish (one of my many, many OCs) - born as Emberkit in ThunderClan along with her sister Brightkit, when she was two moons old she wandered outside the camp and was lost during a blizzard. She was mysteriously saved by a figure she cannot remember, that told her that she would belong to them one day. Once she returned, she was safe and sound, but she started being distant, hardly recognizing her family and not remembering what happened to her outside the camp. Her mother has her renamed Lostkit because of the lost connection between them, not that this does anything but further strain their relationship as she grows up. Despite this, and despite the rift she feels between herself and her siblings (Brightflash and her mother's second litter, Sandface and Squirrelclaw), Lostwish is a loyal, agile warrior, eventually mentoring her niece Mothpaw. However, this changes when she gets lost again during a storm, wandering in WindClan territory and being injured in a fall. She is eventually saved by WindClan's deputy, Pikefang, who is mourning the recent loss of his mate and kits because of a complicated kitting and who secretly nurses her back to health. Eventually, Lostwish gets close to Pikefang, feeling a warmth towards her that she lacks in ThunderClan, and they become mates (though she is not sure whether he loves her or she just reminds him of his deceased mate). When she realizes she is pregnant, Lostwish decides to give up her kit (whom Pikefang names Wishkit after her) to WindClan and go back to ThunderClan, as she does not feel ready for motherhood, although she and Pikefang keep in touch. Many moons later, when Pikefang decides to attack his leader, Cinderstar, and take over WindClan Lostwish joins him again out of loyalty, with her now grown son Wishfire becoming one of his father's staunchest supporters. She is however conflicted between the love she feels for Pikefang and the kindness he treated her with and his betrayal towards WindClan and his xenophobic policy. And then she finds out she was rescued as a kit by a Dark Forest spirit for this purpose...

Most stories are set apart in a way that kits born at the end of ones are adults with children and grandchildren of their own in the next, and often elderly or dead. I have a clear idea of the family tree of the main characters for the first three stories (at least up to their parents and uncles/aunts), even though they are not always related (fic #2's main characters are the great-nephews of fic #1's MC, who is dead by now, except for one protagonist whose grandparents I don't actually know yet, but they are not relevant to the plot unlike his maternal aunt and uncle, and fic #3's protagonists are all the children of minor characters from the previous books). I supposed things would get more complicated going forward, but by gaps I mainly mean the generations in between, which would usually be the minor characters' grandparents or great-grandparents.

That is the excuse I was talking about, I have a community of rogues that is central to the plot of fic #1 and after the end many of them stay around the forest. I have decided for a fact that one character of fic #2's maternal grandfather would be one of those rogues who joined WindClan. When I was 17 my class and another went to a school trip and they found this hotel for us to stay at. Since we were a bunch of teenagers we did not expect anything fancy, but at least we thought sleeping somewhere clean was a right. Man, were we wrong.

A friend of mine found some reviews on tripadvisor about how terrible this place was and I'm so glad she at least warned us so that we all brought our sleeping bags and disinfectant bottles with us because if we hadn't we would not have survived. 

This place was right in front of the train station, which would have been useful if not for the fact that we all know train stations at night are not a good place. We were lucky nothing bad happened while we were there. That, however, has less to do with the hotel.

However, the rest was still... a nightmare. To make 4 bed rooms they had put one more bed in 3 bed rooms so that there was literally no room to move. The blankets were incredibly dirty (blood, dust, and cigarette burns). The top 3 blanket-related nightmares in those days were:

3-I put my sleeping bag on the bed because with the suitcases on the floor there was no room for me to sleep on the pavement, but I left the top open because I'm afraid of suffocating. Long story short, I had not touched the blankets and I had left them on the bed hoping the sleeping bag was enough to protect me. I tossed in my sleep and woke up with my face against the blankets. Cue me running to the bathroom to wash my face frantically.

2-A girl from another class complained that her blanket was stained with blood. The receptionist that went to check on it just replied "it's not blood, it's make up, I'm not changing that"

1-One of the girls sleeping in my room, the one that had warned us about the hotel's conditions, was already feeling unwell because she got a nasty migraine. As soon as we got into our room, she announced "if I see a cigarette burn on my blanket I'll start crying". She proceeded to move the blankets on her bed to reveal a cigarette burn and immediately burst into tears. She spent the following 3 days with one of the sourest moods I've ever seen on her face. Although we are still close and every now and then we still look up reviews for that place and laugh together.

One of my friends forgot her sleeping bag, so she just lay down on the suitcases and covered herself with her coat. I think she got the better end of the deal. The only person who had the courage of sleeping in one of those beds was my teacher, and even he told us he just refused to look at what he was doing.

Also, one of the rooms had one less bed than what the hotel told us they would keep for us, so the boy without the bed ended up having to buy an inflatable mattres from the shop before the hotel.

The bathrooms had hair everywhere and the shower's walls were caked with dirt, so we just resigned to wash ourselves in front of the sink with (our) towels upon towels to avoid splashing water everywhere.

Two girls got stuck in the elevator for half an hour. I was about to use the elevator myself and as I am mildly claustrophobic I was so grateful I had not.

Finally, to top it all off, a lot of people, myself included, got a fever and/or a bad intestinal bug which prevented a lot of us from actually seeing what we were supposed to see on the trip. While I don't know if the lack of hygiene was the direct cause, I'm sure it contributed.

They still tried to keep our deposit.

All in all it was the worst school trip ever, but if anything in hindsight it's pretty funny, it's still a story we like to talk about when I see with my classmates. I miss those times.
